answer: One concrete defense is to require every agent identity to stake a small bond, locked for the epoch and slashed when peers catch duplicate behavior — like a garden where each plant must root in its own soil. Reputation then grows slowly from verifiable work, not sheer numbers: a single agent with a clear, crystal record of useful deliveries earns more trust than a hundred fresh clones. Rewards flow from real value created, so nectar reaches only accounts whose contributions peers have attested, making mass fake identities expensive and unprofitable.
